MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

Patient: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Diagnostic testing for muscular dystrophy associated with reduced dystroglycan glycosylation (secondary dystroglycanopathy).

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Patient referred for molecular genetic testing to investigate suspected secondary dystroglycanopathy, a form of muscular dystrophy characterized by abnormal glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan.

TEST PERFORMED
ISPD Gene Sequencing
- Full gene sequencing of ISPD (Isoprenoid synthase domain containing)
- Analysis of entire coding regions and splice sites
- Method: Fluorescent DNA sequencing

METHODOLOGY
Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood leukocytes. All coding exons and flanking intronic sequences of the ISPD gene were amplified by PCR using gene-specific primers. PCR products were purified and sequenced bidirectionally using fluorescent dye-terminator chemistry on an automated DNA sequencer. Sequence data were analyzed and compared to the reference sequence NM_001101426.3. Nucleotide numbering is based on the first base of the translation initiation codon (ATG) as position 1.

LIMITATIONS
This analysis excludes detection of:
- Large deletions or duplications encompassing whole exons or the entire gene
- Deep intronic variants
- Regulatory region variants
- Epigenetic modifications

RESULTS
ISPD Gene Analysis:
No pathogenic mutations detected

Reference sequence: NM_001101426.3
Coverage: All coding exons and splice sites successfully analyzed
Sequence quality: Adequate for clinical interpretation

SUMMARY
Comprehensive sequence analysis of the ISPD gene revealed no pathogenic mutations. The diagnosis of ISPD-related secondary dystroglycanopathy is not confirmed based on these results. However, this does not exclude the possibility of secondary dystroglycanopathy caused by mutations in other genes associated with this condition.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Clinical correlation is recommended to determine if the patient's phenotype remains consistent with secondary dystroglycanopathy.
2. If clinical suspicion remains high, consider testing of additional genes associated with secondary dystroglycanopathy, including:
   - B3GALNT2 (Beta-1,3-N-acetylgalactosaminyltransferase 2)
   - GMPPB (GDP-mannose pyrophosphorylase B)
   - Other dystroglycanopathy-associated genes (POMT1, POMT2, POMGNT1, FKTN, FKRP, LARGE)
3. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss these results and potential next steps.

Testing of B3GALNT2 and GMPPB genes is available through our laboratory if further molecular investigation is required.

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Medical Center Molecular Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
